sections.title: Who is it for?

q.prompt: Which word means “the group of people an advert is made for”?
q.reason: “target audience” means the group of people an advert is made for.

options.fb: “brand” means the name a company uses for its products.
“purpose” means the reason why something is made.

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 7. In this lesson: Who is it for?
Identify target audience and purpose in an advert.
Here are some new words. Target audience. The group of people an advert is made for. Brand.
The name a company uses for its products. Purpose. The reason why something is made.
And some more words. Appeal. Make people interested or want something. Logo.
A small design that represents a company. Feature. An important part or quality of a product.
Time for a question. The video will stop. Which word means: the group of people an advert is made for?
Now some grammar: Comparatives and superlatives in adverts. Adverts often use comparatives (faster,
more powerful) and superlatives (the best, the most exciting) to make products seem special.
For example: Now 50 phần trăm faster! For example: The most comfortable trainers ever.
Now listen, and read along. ZoomRun trainers.
ZoomRun X – Run Further, Feel Lighter Are you ready to beat your best time?
The new ZoomRun X is our lightest trainer ever – 20 phần trăm lighter than last year's model.
Its special foam gives you more bounce with every step, so you feel less tired on long runs.
Designed with young athletes, it comes in five bold colours.
‘I ran my fastest 5 K ever in ZoomRun X!’ – Kai, 14, junior champion Only at Sportz stores.
Students get 15 phần trăm off with a school I D.
Another question. The video will stop. What is being advertised?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like target audience, brand, purpose.
You practised comparatives and superlatives in adverts. And you read ZoomRun trainers.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!

options.t: that the juice helps you think faster

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 7. In this lesson: Reading between the lines.
Analyse persuasive tricks and decide how reliable an advert is.
Here are some new words. Claim. A statement that something is true, which may not be proved. Testimonial.
A statement from a customer praising a product. Small print. The detailed rules written in tiny letters.
And some more words. Misleading. Giving the wrong idea. Critical. Thinking carefully and asking questions.
Consumer. A person who buys things.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: a statement that something is true, which may not be proved?
Now some grammar: Hedging and vague language.
Adverts sometimes use vague words like ‘up to’, ‘helps’ and ‘may’ so that their claims are hard to prove.
For example: ‘Up to 50 phần trăm off’ (maybe only one item!). For example: ‘Helps you feel more energetic’.
For example: ‘May improve your skin’.
Now listen, and read along. Brain Boost Juice. Brain Boost Juice Want better grades?
Brain Boost Juice helps you think faster!
Packed with natural fruit, it may improve your focus during exams.
‘After one week of Brain Boost, I got an A in science!’ – Sophie, 13 Up to 50 phần trăm off this weekend!
Small print: Offer applies to selected 2-litre bottles only. Contains 30 g of added sugar per bottle.
These claims have not been tested in a scientific study.
Another question. The video will stop. What does the advert promise?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like claim, testimonial, small print.
You practised hedging and vague language. And you read Brain Boost Juice. Now try the practice questions.
See you next time!
